title: Swim in Rising Water
description:
You are given an n x n integer matrix grid where each value grid[i][j] represents the elevation at that point (i, j).

Rain starts to fall. At time t, the depth of the water everywhere is t. You can swim from a square to another 4-directionally adjacent square if and only if the elevation of both squares individually are at most t. You can swim infinite distances in zero time. Of course, you must stay within the boundaries of the grid during your swim.

Return the least time until you can reach the bottom right square (n - 1, n - 1) if you start at the top left square (0, 0).

examples.explanation: At time 0, you are in grid location (0, 0). You cannot go anywhere else because 4-directionally adjacent neighbors have a higher elevation than t = 0. You cannot reach point (1, 1) until time 3. When the depth of water is 3, we can swim anywhere inside the grid.
The final route is shown; we need to wait until time 16 so that (0, 0) and (4, 4) are connected.

approach: The cost of a path is the maximum elevation encountered along it, and we want the path from the top-left to the bottom-right that minimizes this bottleneck value. This bottleneck cost is monotone under path extension, so Dijkstra's algorithm applies: relax each neighbor with next_cost = max(current_cost, neighbor_height) instead of a sum. Seed a min-heap with the start cell's elevation, and pop cells in increasing finalized cost; the first time the destination is finalized, that cost is the earliest time you can reach it. For an n x n grid there are n^2 vertices and O(n^2) edges, giving O(n^2 log n) time. A binary-search + flood-fill or a Union-Find that unites cells in increasing elevation order also solves it.
